To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AI has been used in a wide range of tasks and industries, with some success, but there are many challenges ahead.

(1) the automation of jobs and the restructuring of the world of labour are not new phenomena; (2) they have been a constant in the history of the world of work; (3) the current phase of automation is more complex and dynamic than ever, due to its technological, economic and social characteristics; (4) the impact of these processes on the labour force is very heterogeneous, and depends on the sector of the economy, the country, the type of work, etc.; and

1) AI is not a new phenomenon; 2) AI has been used to automate work since its inception; 3) AI is currently being used to automate work at scale, in a variety of industries; 4) AI is being used to automate a range of work tasks, including cognitive, physical, and social work; 5) AI is currently having a limited impact on work, but its impact is growing rapidly, and will likely grow even more rapidly as AI capabilities improve
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the specific applications of AI in the world of labour?
the following issues: 1.
two main questions: (1) how do we conceptualize the relationship between automation and restructuring?; and (2) what is the role of AI in the current phase of capitalist development?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AI revolution, in the sense of the automation of the labour process, is not a reality.
AI is not a single, monolithic technology.
the AI revolution will not be a revolution, at least not a revolutionary one, and that the future of work will not be determined by AI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it seeks to contribute to the debate on the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) and automation on the world of labour and, in particular, on the capitalist restructuring process.
it is a critical analysis of the current state of the question on automation, AI and the future of work, based on the review of a significant part of the literature on the topic.
the development of new technologies has been a key element in the restructuring processes in capitalism, but the current phase seems to be different from previous ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the AI and automation literature is dominated by two main perspectives: the first one, which is the dominant one, is the techno-optimist one, which is based on the idea that AI and automation will bring about a bright new future for all of us.
, while AI is not a panacea for all the problems facing society and the world of labour, it is also not a monster that will destroy the world of labour and the working classes.
the current wave of AI is not a novelty in the history of capitalism.
